tasks.title: Retain the frozen frame's raw PNG bytes as a HeldFrame (one value, one read)
tasks.description: Introduce a private internal data class HeldFrame(bitmap: ImageBitmap, bytes: ByteArray) in MirrorViewModel backed by one MutableStateFlow<HeldFrame?> for the live frame and one for the frozen frame. observeFrames' map stage currently discards the captured MirrorFrameModel at MirrorViewModel.kt:219-223 after decoding it into an ImageBitmap; carry it through so the collect body constructs exactly one HeldFrame per frame. stageAnnotation must read the live holder with exactly ONE .value read and copy it into the frozen holder at the same moment currentFrozenFrame is set, so frame.png is guaranteed to be the pixels the user annotated. The public frame: StateFlow<ImageBitmap?> keeps its existing type and is assigned from the same collect body; nothing else pairs off it. resumeLive/stopSession/selectPlatform clear both holders with the frame. HeldFrame must never enter MirrorUiState (reduced state stays pixel-free per presentation-feature-mirror/CLAUDE.md deviation 2).

acceptanceCriteria.text: A fake transport emitting two frames with distinguishable bytes and distinguishable bitmaps proves the frozen HeldFrame's bitmap and bytes come from the SAME frame, never a mix (the read-atomicity invariant).
frame.png eventually assembled from this bytes field is byte-identical to the original adb-captured bytes — no decode/re-encode round trip.
HeldFrame and its bytes do not appear anywhere in MirrorUiState (grep-level check).

references.ref: presentation-feature-mirror/src/commonMain/kotlin/presentation/feature/mirror/source/mirror/MirrorViewModel.kt:210-225 (observeFrames), :353-356 (stageAnnotation freeze)
data-device-impl/.../source/DeviceSourcesProvider.kt — the PNG-signature trim precedent that makes frame.png a byte copy

tasks.expectedOutput: MirrorViewModel.kt edited in place: new private HeldFrame class, two private StateFlow<HeldFrame?> holders, observeFrames and stageAnnotation updated, plus a commonTest proving the pairing invariant with a two-distinguishable-frames fake.
tasks.hypothesis: Pairing bitmap+bytes as ONE value on ONE StateFlow makes both the write and the read atomic; two co-assigned separate flows would leave stageAnnotation performing two independent .value reads that a newly arrived frame can straddle, silently mismatching frame.png against the annotated pixels.

tasks.title: Create :data-handoff-api — envelope, AnnotationHandoff, FileSlotAnnotationHandoff, factory, settings.gradle.kts, CLAUDE.md, and its full desktopTest suite
tasks.description: New library-convention-plugin Gradle module :data-handoff-api (+ libs.plugins.kotlin.serialization, no di plugin — deliberately Koin-free so :mcp-application's classpath stays envelope+serialization only). commonMain: source/envelope/AnnotationEnvelope.kt (@Serializable, version: Int FIRST field, plus EnvelopeDevice/EnvelopeAnnotation/HandoffImage per the plan's dataModel) and source/handoff/AnnotationHandoff.kt (ONE public interface — declared deviation 1 from preparation's two-interface wording — with suspend publish(envelope, images), suspend latest(): AnnotationEnvelope?, and resolve(envelope, name): String). desktopMain (internal): core/slot/FileSlotAnnotationHandoff.kt implementing the interface via temp-write + Files.move(ATOMIC_MOVE, REPLACE_EXISTING) to <root>/latest.json, images written to <root>/<sentAtMs>/<name> BEFORE the move, pruning every sibling numeric directory latest.json does not name after each publish, owner-only POSIX permissions on <root> where supported, and resolve() rejecting any name containing '/' or '..' before composing a file:// URI (the slot is untrusted input even though Rectify wrote it). source/handoff/FileSlotFactory.kt: public fun fileSlotAnnotationHandoff(root: Path = defaultHandoffRoot()) — root is the test seam. Register the module in settings.gradle.kts under the // data group, and write an initial data-handoff-api/CLAUDE.md describing the module's responsibility (expanded later in T-12's documentation pass).

acceptanceCriteria.text: publish then latest() returns an equal envelope by content (not identity).
latest() called twice with no publish in between returns byte-identical/equal-content envelopes (AC-81 at the storage layer).
A second publish replaces the slot and the old per-send directory is pruned.
An absent slot returns null from latest(), never an exception.
version survives the round trip and is the FIRST key in the serialized JSON (AC-32).
Image bytes round-trip byte-identically at <root>/<sentAtMs>/<name>.
resolve() rejects any name containing '/' or '..'.
latest.json.tmp does not survive a successful publish; any latest.json present on disk always parses.
A garbage latest.json yields null-or-error, never an exception escaping latest().

references.ref: data-core/CLAUDE.md — 'No external dependencies allowed — this module is a leaf', the evidence the envelope cannot live there
desktop-application/build.gradle.kts + desktop-application/CLAUDE.md — the plain-JVM/bespoke-Gradle precedent this module's library-convention build.gradle.kts does NOT need to deviate from
plan.json#architecture.interfaces 'AnnotationHandoff' and 'data-handoff-api/build.gradle.kts' for the exact contract and build file

tasks.expectedOutput: New :data-handoff-api module with commonMain envelope+interface, desktopMain FileSlotAnnotationHandoff+factory, settings.gradle.kts include, data-handoff-api/CLAUDE.md, and a desktopTest suite covering publish/read/read-again identity, replacement+prune, absent slot, version round trip, path-traversal rejection, and no surviving .tmp.

tasks.title: Implement the MirrorViewModel send handler with the four constructor seams; wire Koin; update MirrorFakes
tasks.description: Append four constructor parameters in decodeFrame's existing style: private val handoff: AnnotationHandoff (REQUIRED, no default — defaulting it would turn a missing Koin binding into a silent runtime no-op), private val encodeCrop: CropEncoder = CropEncoder { _, _ -> null }, private val nowMs: () -> Long = { Clock.System.now().toEpochMilliseconds() }, private val elapsed: TimeSource = TimeSource.Monotonic. Handle MirrorIntent.ResolveAndSend: guard on canSend(state); guard separately on the frozen HeldFrame being present and reduce SendPhase.Failed with a Kermit warning if absent (canSend cannot see bytes; a silent no-op on an enabled button is worse than a visible failure); reduce SendPhase.Preparing, assemble the envelope off the main thread via EnvelopeAssembly, reduce SendPhase.Publishing, call handoff.publish, measure elapsed with the injected monotonic seam; on success capture stagedCount BEFORE resetting, post SendComplete, resume live UNLESS the session is Lost (SC-27), and clear the staged batch (FR-19/AC-21); on failure reduce SendPhase.Failed and leave the frozen frame, its HeldFrame bytes and the staged list untouched (AS-31/AC-20/SC-25). Wire via Koin using viewModel { MirrorViewModel(...) } with explicit get<T>() calls (never viewModelOf) at PresentationFeatureMirrorModule.kt:24-25, and update MirrorFakes.kt:271's fake construction site.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A second ResolveAndSend while in flight is dropped (reducer guard, the Cmd+Enter path's backstop).
A ResolveAndSend at zero staged is dropped.
Success resumes live and resets the counter to 0, reading stagedCount BEFORE the reset so the toast reports the pre-reset count.
Success while the session is Lost does NOT resume live (SC-27) — frame stays pinned, toast still confirms.
Failure leaves the frozen frame, its HeldFrame bytes and the annotation list unchanged, and re-enables the button (AS-31/AC-20/SC-25).
A send with no HeldFrame reduces SendPhase.Failed with a Kermit warning rather than returning silently.
No assembly, encoding or file write runs on the main dispatcher (AS-30, review check).

tasks.title: Create :mcp-application — bespoke build.gradle.kts, Main.kt read loop, McpDispatcher, tool-result rendering, and its pure String->String tests
tasks.description: New plain-JVM module (no convention plugin — all four model KotlinMultiplatformExtension, so this extends :desktop-application's already-documented bespoke-Gradle precedent by one, per decision 6's human gate): plugins { alias(libs.plugins.kotlinJvm); alias(libs.plugins.kotlin.serialization); application }, jvmToolchain(21), implementation(projects.dataHandoffApi) + libs.kotlinx.serialization.json only (no Compose/Koin/Skiko), testImplementation(kotlin("test")) (sanctioned per-module exception — this module has no convention plugin to wire it once). mainClass dev.rectify.io.mcp.source.entry.MainKt, applicationName "rectify-mcp". McpDispatcher.kt (internal): a pure suspend fun handle(line: String): String? over an injected AnnotationHandoff — null means 'notification, write nothing' — dispatching initialize (echo MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION), notifications/initialized, tools/list (exactly one tool, get_latest_annotation, empty object inputSchema), tools/call -> get_latest_annotation (metadata+prompt+hierarchy inline, images by file:// reference per decision 8; empty slot -> explicit 'No annotation has been sent yet.' text with isError false; newer envelope version -> isError true naming BOTH version numbers plus the rebuild command; corrupt slot -> isError true with the parse message, never throws). Main.kt: runBlocking { generateSequence(::readLine).forEach { dispatcher.handle(it)?.let(::writeFrame) } }, exit 0 on stdin EOF; writeFrame is the ONLY function in the module touching System.out — every diagnostic goes to System.err via a stderr helper, logging the resolved handoff root once at startup. Register :mcp-application in settings.gradle.kts.

A corrupt slot yields a tool error and the function still returns rather than throwing out of the loop.
Every dispatcher response is exactly one line with no embedded newline (the stdout-corruption guard).

tasks.title: Cross-target build gate and the mandatory manual end-to-end demo against a real Claude Code session
tasks.description: Run the cross-target build gate: ./gradlew :presentation-feature-mirror:build :data-handoff-api:build :mcp-application:build --max-workers=1 (bugs.json#PP-TD-8: the Kotlin/Native release linker OOMs under parallel linkReleaseFramework tasks — use --max-workers=1, do not chase it as a defect introduced by this spec) plus :presentation-feature-mirror:desktopTest :data-handoff-api:desktopTest :mcp-application:test. A green desktop suite alone does not count — commonTest compiles for every target and Kotlin/Native is stricter than the JVM. Then perform and RECORD the mandatory manual demo, which CI provably cannot cover: ./gradlew :mcp-application:installDist; add the documented .mcp.json.example entry to a real Claude Code MCP config; run the desktop app against a real Android device or AVD; stage annotations; click Resolve & Send (and separately verify Cmd+Enter); watch the StatusLine sequence Streaming -> Frozen -> Dumping hierarchy -> Sent and the completion toast with its 'Open session' clipboard action; have a real Claude Code session call get_latest_annotation and receive the payload; call it a second time with no new send in between and confirm an identical result (AC-81). Record the transcript, the measured end-to-end elapsed time against the <=2s NFR-3 target, and the inline tool-result byte size against the 512 KB budget, in the execution report.
